full_judgment:
Mainur Reza Chowdhury, J: These civil appeals arise out of the judgment and decree dated 23.2.2000 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 85 of 1997 and First Appeal No. 158 of 1999 affirming the judgment and decree dated 24.3.1997 passed by the Subordinate Judge and First Commercial Court at Dhaka in Title Suit No. 1 of 1996 filed by the plaintiff-respondent No. 1. These two civil appeals have arisen out of the same judgment of the High Court Division in the above mentioned First Appeals which were heard together and disposed of by one judgment. The defendants Nos. 1 and 3 in the title suit are the appellants, and the plaintiff is the respondent No. 1 in these two civil appeals before us. 

 2. Facts relevant for the purpose of these two civil appeals are that the plaintiff-respondent No. 1, Rahimafrooz Batteries Ltd. is successor-in-interest of Lucas Service (Pakistan) Limited, conducting the business of manufacture of batteries in the ground floor of holding. No. 74, Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka since 1961. Like the plaintiffs predecessor-in-interest the plaintiff was accepted as monthly tenant in the ground  floor in the aforesaid building. While the plaintiff was running business in the said building the holding was declared as an abandoned property under President's Order No. 16 of 1972 and it vested in the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, defendant No. 1. The defendant No.1 also recognized plaintiff Rahimafrooz Batteries Ltd. as tenant of the ground floor of the building by accepting monthly rent. Rent was enhanced to Tk.8935/- per month. The Government i.e. defendant No. 1 intended to disinvest the holding No.74, Motijheel Commercial Area and invited tenders from the intending purchasers on terms and conditions laid down in the tender. The plaintiff being one of the tenants of the suit holding submitted tender for purchasing the building by depositing earnest money of Tk. 1,75,050.00. The appellant in Civil Appeal No. 139 of 2002, namely, United Commercial Bank Ltd., who was defendant No.3 in the suit, also submitted a tender offering Tk. 1,21,01,100/-. The offer of the defendant No.3 being the highest it was accepted by defendant No. 1, the Government of Bangladesh. Then notices were issued on the tenants asking them to surrender possession of their respective tenanted portion of the holding to the Superintending Engineer, Management Circle of the Ministry of Works by 6.7.1986 failing which they would be evicted on any, subsequent date. The plaintiff alleged that on receipt of such a notice he came to know that the tender of defendant No.3 was accepted. So he filed the above Title Suit No.1 of 1996 against the appellants praying for a decree that plaintiff's tender for purchase of the suit property was still subsisting and that the plaintiff was entitled to purchase the same on the same terms and conditions as those of defendant No.3 and the defendant No.1 was hound to sell the same to the plaintiff on the same terms and conditions and that acceptance of the tender of defendant No.3 was "illegal and no longer valid and binding upon the plaintiff." The plaintiff being tenant in possession of part of the suit holding was entitled to purchase the suit holding at the highest price quoted in the tender. It was stated by the plaintiff that one of the conditions of the tender form was that the earnest money of the unsuccessful tenderer would be refunded within one month from the date of the decision regarding acceptance of the tender. As the plaintiffs earnest money had not been refunded it was presumed that the tender of the plaintiff had not been refused and the same was under consideration of the defendant No:1. Since the plaintiff was an existing tenant in the suit holding (building) the plaintiff s tender and offer to buy the holding at the highest price offered by defendant No.3 had to be accepted by defendant No. 1. The defendants No. 1 and 2 and the defendant No.3 filed two separate written statements before the trial court. It was stated that according to the rules the property in question was sold through tender to the highest offered defendant No. 3. Since the tender was floated according to the Rules and the defendant No. 1 accepted the offer of the highest tender of defendant No. 3 the plaintiff had no claim for purchasing the suit property. The offer of the highest tenderer, defendant No. 3, i.e. United Commercial Bank Ltd., having been accepted the contract was complete and the plaintiff was not entitled to claim any right to purchase the suit holding. 

 3. The trial court decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff to the effect that the defendants No.1 and 2 were bound to sell the suit holding to the plaintiff at the highest tender money as offered by the highest tenderer, defendant No. 3. Being aggrieved the defendant No.3 the highest tenderer preferred First Appeal No. 85 of 1997 and defendants No. 1 and 2 preferred First Appeal No. 158 of 1999 before the High Court Division. The High Court Division dismissed the two appeals and maintained the decree passed by the trial court. 

 12. We therefore, entertain no doubt that the Act of 1963 is retrospective in the sense that it applies to proceedings pending at the time when the Act came into force. Accordingly it only remains to consider whether this Court in the exercise of its appellate jurisdiction can substitute for the judgment and order of the High Court a judgment or order in accordance with the law as now exists without discussing the law as it existed at the time when the High Court had seisin of the case. Once an appeal has been admitted against the decree or order of the High Court, the matter becomes subjoined again and thereafter this Court has seisin of the whole case. This Court therefore, can take into account the provisions of the new Act which repealed the Act of 1957 and grant relief accordingly even though the judgment of the High Court had been correct according to law as it then stood." 

 12. The appeals are therefore allowed without any order as to costs and the judgment and decree dated 23.2.2000 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 85 of 1977 and First Appeal No. 158 of 1999 affirming the judgment and decree dated-24.3.1997 passed by the Subordinate Judge and First Commercial Court at Dhaka in Title Suit No.1 of 1996 are hereby set aside.
